headline: TTWO surges nearly 6%, Alphabet soars on strong Q2 earnings — but PLS and GXAI drag the ASX holdings lower today.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two jumped nearly 6% last night on no specific breaking news — the move likely reflects broader momentum and renewed appetite for gaming stocks. The long-term thesis around Grand Theft Auto VI and its massive release pipeline remains intact.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS fell almost 5% in today's session, giving back recent gains. Despite a global report showing H1 lithium prices surging over 130% year-on-year, the ASX lithium sector pulled back today — likely profit-taking after recent strength. The fundamental lithium price story is improving, but volatility remains high.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 3.2% today, likely tracking a softer ASX session for tech-adjacent stocks. The NASDAQ fell last night and that sentiment carried through. No specific news on the ETF itself — this is normal day-to-day noise for an AI-focused fund.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet surged 2.3% last night after posting excellent Q2 earnings — revenue hit $119.8 billion, well above expectations. The market shrugged off concerns about AI capital spending (capex) and rewarded the strong results. Google also announced Pixel price increases, signalling confidence in its hardware brand.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 1.9% last night ahead of its Q2 earnings report due Wednesday US time. The market is pricing in optimism, with analysts watching whether Azure cloud growth can justify Microsoft's enormous $220 billion AI infrastructure spend. Expect a sharp move either way post-earnings.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 1% today in a quiet session. Emerging markets faced a slight headwind as the Aussie dollar softened a touch and broader risk appetite was cautious. China's economic resilience data was positive, but not enough to lift the ETF today.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.5% today on the ASX, reflecting the NASDAQ's weakness last night (down 0.82%). The S&P 500 was essentially flat, so this is minor noise — nothing structurally changed.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped just 0.25% today — barely a blip. As a diversified fund across global and Australian shares, bonds, and property, daily moves this small are completely normal. Nothing to see here.

watch_today.title: Microsoft earnings drop Wednesday US time — big swing coming for MSFT
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports Q2 earnings Wednesday night (US) — that's Thursday morning AEST. Analysts are watching whether Azure cloud revenue growth can justify the company's eye-watering $220 billion AI capex (capital spending) plan. Markets are pricing in a ~7% swing either way. You're currently down 12% on MSFT overall. If earnings disappoint, there may be short-term pain — but for a long-term holder, the Azure + AI story is still very much intact. Sit tight and wait for the result.

watch_today.title: TTWO surging — long-term case strengthening
watch_today.detail: Take-Two jumped nearly 6% last night, pushing your position into profit (+5% overall). No single news catalyst, but gaming sector sentiment is improving as the GTA VI release window gets closer. For a long-term holder this is a good sign — hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: PLS down nearly 5% today — but lithium fundamentals are turning
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell 4.9% in today's session and you're now down 40% overall on this position. However, a major industry report out today shows global H1 lithium prices surged over 130% year-on-year, with some miners' profits up 4,900%. The long-term recovery story is building — this dip looks like sector noise, not a structural break. Hold unless your conviction in lithium has changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI down 3.2% today — still underwater overall
watch_today.detail: The AI ETF dropped another 3.2% today, and you're now down over 20% on this position. The day's move tracks NASDAQ weakness from last night rather than any AI-specific bad news. The broader AI investment theme remains very active (Nvidia launching a new security alliance, Google posting record revenues). For a long-term holder, hold — but be aware this one needs patience.

watch_today.title: Alphabet had a blinder — GOOG in the green
watch_today.detail: Google's parent Alphabet reported Q2 revenue of $119.8 billion, smashing expectations. The stock jumped 2.3% last night and you're now up 6.2% on your position. No action needed — the AI ad-revenue flywheel is firing. Hold with confidence.

watch_today.title: RBA governor issues candid warning on living standards — watch for rate cut signals
watch_today.detail: RBA Governor Michele Bullock today acknowledged the housing market has eased 'more than anticipated' and sounded the alarm on a slump in Australians' living standards. This is unusually candid language from the RBA and could signal more interest rate cuts ahead — which is generally good for growth assets like your shares and ETFs. Watch for any RBA meeting updates this week.

world.summary: The Middle East remains on edge as the US and Iran pause strikes for a third night to allow diplomacy to proceed. Trump's administration pushes the Supreme Court on mail-in voting rules ahead of midterms. Australia faces potential fuel price pain as Middle East tensions disrupt oil supply, and China posts resilient economic data boosting global confidence.

stories.title: US and Iran pause strikes for third consecutive night to allow peace talks
stories.why_it_matters: The US and Iran have now held off on strikes for three nights running, creating a diplomatic window for negotiations. Trump told reporters the two sides are having 'good talks', while drones have continued to hit Iran's neighbouring countries — keeping the region on edge. A fragile ceasefire is in place, but oil markets are watching closely; crude dropped over 2.5% last night, partly on hopes the conflict won't escalate further. For everyday Australians, any sustained Middle East conflict risks higher petrol prices at the bowser.

stories.title: Australia faces potential fuel pain — and may build its first oil refinery in 60 years
stories.why_it_matters: Middle East tensions are pushing Australian fuel prices higher, with Treasurer Jim Chalmers warning of inflation risks from the conflict. In response, there is now serious talk of building Australia's first domestic oil refinery in 60 years — a major shift in energy security policy. Australia currently imports almost all its refined fuel, making it acutely vulnerable to global supply shocks. Higher petrol costs hit household budgets directly and add to broader inflation pressure the RBA is already fighting.

stories.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to allow order restricting mail-in voting before midterms
stories.source: The New York Times / The Guardian
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is pushing the US Supreme Court to allow an executive order that would restrict mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections. A lower appeals court has already blocked the order, but the administration is appealing urgently. Critics argue it's an attempt to suppress votes from demographics that lean Democratic; supporters say it's about election integrity. This is shaping up as one of the biggest legal battles of the US political calendar — and the Supreme Court's decision could reshape how millions of Americans vote.

stories.title: Salzburg Summit 2026: World leaders and business elite gather to reshape global alliances
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 Salzburg Summit has brought together world political leaders and the economic elite under the theme 'Alliances in a New Global Order' — a direct response to shifting US foreign policy, the rise of China, and the fragmentation of traditional Western alliances. The summit signals how countries and corporations are actively rethinking trade, security, and economic partnerships. For investors, the realignment of global alliances has direct implications for supply chains, emerging markets, and the value of international ETFs like VGE.

stories.title: China's economic resilience boosts global confidence
stories.why_it_matters: Fresh data shows China's economy is holding up better than feared despite trade tensions and a sluggish property market, boosting confidence in global growth. This is directly relevant if you hold VGE (Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF), which has significant China exposure. A stronger Chinese economy supports demand for Australian resources including lithium and iron ore, which matters for holdings like Pilbara Minerals.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 closed up 0.6% today, a solid session driven by broad-based gains. Last night in the US, the S&P 500 was virtually flat (+0.07%) while the NASDAQ dropped 0.82% — a divergence driven by rotation out of some tech names after a big run-up. Crude oil fell sharply (down 2.55%) on hopes for a US-Iran diplomatic resolution. Gold slipped slightly. The Aussie dollar dipped marginally to 69.73 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — up 0.6% to close near 8,948.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — the market is holding its breath ahead of big tech earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ slipped 0.82% last night as some tech names pulled back after recent strength.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell over 2.5% last night on cautious optimism that the US-Iran standoff may ease through diplomacy.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold edged down slightly as risk appetite held up and safe-haven demand eased a touch.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to just under 70 US cents — a minor move, no major catalyst.

politics.summary: The RBA is making headlines today with an unusually candid warning from Governor Michele Bullock about falling living standards and a housing market that has cooled faster than expected. Rate cut signals are growing. Meanwhile, the Albanese government faces political pressure on several domestic policy fronts.

stories.title: RBA Governor Bullock sounds alarm on Australia's falling living standards
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Governor Michele Bullock has issued what commentators are calling an unusually candid warning: Australia's living standards are in a genuine slump, and the housing market has cooled 'more than anticipated'. This language from the top of the Reserve Bank strongly hints that further interest rate cuts could be on the table — good news for mortgage holders and borrowers. Lower rates generally support share prices and reduce pressure on household budgets. Watch for RBA commentary over the coming weeks.

stories.title: Housing market cooled faster than expected, RBA confirms
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has formally acknowledged in its latest communications that Australia's housing market has eased more sharply than its own models predicted. This is significant because it suggests the rate hikes of recent years have done their job — and possibly overcorrected. For renters and first-home buyers, softer property prices offer some relief. For property investors, it raises questions about near-term capital growth prospects.

stories.title: 'Part of the plan': RBA makes grim admission on rates strategy
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has effectively admitted that the pain inflicted on Australian households through interest rate hikes was deliberate — a calculated strategy to crush inflation. News.com.au reports the bank is describing the housing slowdown and consumer squeeze as 'part of the plan'. This admission is politically awkward for both the RBA and the Albanese government, as many Australians have struggled significantly under higher mortgage repayments over the past two years.

stories.title: Albanese faces policy minefields: 'divorce tax', death tax and Widows Tax
stories.why_it_matters: Political commentators are warning that the Albanese government needs to defuse several politically toxic 'landmines' — including proposed changes that critics are calling a 'secret divorce tax', death duty concerns, and ongoing controversy over the so-called Widows Tax (a rule that cuts pension income for some surviving spouses). While some of these labels are contested, they represent a PR challenge for Labor as it manages both welfare reform and cost-of-living politics simultaneously.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Nvidia and Microsoft launching a new Open Secure AI Alliance with 37 companies — but notably without OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic. Separately, Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro is still MIA despite being announced months ago, and China's Moonshot is releasing its Kimi K3 model to the public. The EU's AI Omnibus regulation has come into force with eased deadlines.

stories.title: Nvidia and Microsoft launch AI security alliance — but OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are all absent
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia and Microsoft have formed the 'Open Secure AI Alliance' with 37 member companies — essentially a framework to make AI systems safer and harder to hack. But the three biggest AI labs — OpenAI, Google/DeepMind, and Anthropic — are all conspicuously absent. This came after a reported security breach of an OpenAI AI agent, which likely accelerated the push for the alliance. The split raises questions about whether AI safety efforts will be fragmented, with the biggest players doing their own thing. For GOOG and MSFT holders, this is worth watching — Microsoft is inside the tent, Google is not.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro is still missing — announced at Google I/O but nowhere to be seen
stories.why_it_matters: Google announced Gemini 3.5 Pro — an upgraded AI model — at its big Google I/O developer conference months ago, but it still hasn't shipped. Mashable reports the model is simply 'MIA' (missing in action), which is raising eyebrows in the tech community. For a company that just posted $119.8 billion in quarterly revenue and is leaning heavily on its AI narrative, delays in flagship AI model releases could give rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI time to pull further ahead. Worth watching as a risk for GOOG holders.

stories.title: China's Moonshot to release Kimi K3 — a powerful AI model available for public download
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is about to release its latest flagship model, Kimi K3, as a freely downloadable open-weights model — meaning anyone can run it on their own hardware. This continues the pattern of Chinese AI labs releasing powerful open models to compete with Western closed-source systems like GPT-4 and Claude. It puts further pressure on the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic to justify their premium pricing, and keeps the global AI race intensely competitive.

stories.title: EU's AI Omnibus regulation enters into force with extended deadlines and easier compliance rules
stories.why_it_matters: The European Union's updated AI Omnibus regulation — a sweeping set of rules governing how AI systems can be used and developed — has officially come into force. Crucially, the final version includes extended compliance deadlines and easier requirements for businesses, a win for tech companies that had lobbied heavily against the original stricter draft. This matters for global tech companies like Google and Microsoft who operate in Europe — less regulatory friction means fewer compliance costs and fewer restrictions on their AI products in one of the world's biggest markets.

stories.title: Andrew Forrest warns: regulate AI or be 'naive to extinction'
stories.why_it_matters: Billionaire Andrew Forrest has issued a stark warning at a public forum: without proper regulation, AI development is leading humanity toward extinction-level risks. He urged governments to act decisively, comparing inaction to wilful naivety. Forrest joins a growing chorus of tech and business heavyweights — including figures at major AI labs — calling for guardrails. The comments add to the regulatory pressure building globally around AI, which could ultimately affect how and how fast companies like Google and Microsoft can deploy their AI products.

sport.summary: NRL Round 22 team lists are out with a couple of notable shocks, including a big blow for the Broncos. The AFL ladder race is tightening with Melbourne suffering a costly loss. Darts legend Luke Littler is drawing Phil Taylor comparisons after a record-breaking win at Blackpool.

stories.title: Broncos lose star to season-ending injury; Tigers make shock Doueihi call for Round 22
stories.why_it_matters: The Brisbane Broncos have copped a major blow heading into Round 22, with a key player's season confirmed over due to injury — a significant hit to their premiership ambitions. Meanwhile the Wests Tigers have made a shock selection call, recalling Adam Doueihi in what's described as a surprise move. Round 22 kicks off Thursday night with Cowboys vs Roosters at 7:50pm, and the Titans host the Warriors at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday at 3pm — right in your backyard on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Perth Bears poach another Panthers premiership player for the NRL's new WA franchise
stories.why_it_matters: The Perth Bears, the NRL's incoming new franchise, have signed another premiership-winning Penrith Panthers player as they build their squad ahead of their debut season. This is part of a broader talent drain from the Panthers dynasty as their salary cap forces them to let go of quality players. The Bears' signings are attracting serious attention — they look set to be competitive from day one.

stories.title: PNG Chiefs NRL bid: Zac Lomax signs as PM Marape hails 'nation building' project
stories.why_it_matters: Papua New Guinea's bid for an NRL franchise — the PNG Chiefs — is gaining serious momentum, with star player Zac Lomax now confirmed as a signing. PNG Prime Minister James Marape described the project as 'nation building', and Australian federal funding has been discussed as part of the broader Pacific engagement strategy. If the Chiefs get the green light, it would be a historic expansion of the NRL into PNG — a nation where rugby league is the dominant sport.

stories.title: Luke Littler draws Phil Taylor comparisons after record-breaking World Matchplay victory at Blackpool
stories.why_it_matters: Teen darts sensation Luke Littler has won the World Matchplay at Blackpool in historic fashion, breaking records in the process and prompting legends of the sport to draw direct comparisons with the greatest darts player of all time, Phil Taylor. Littler, still in his teens, is rapidly becoming one of the most compelling sporting stories in the world — a generational talent who is redefining what's possible in the sport.

stories.title: AFL ladder race tightens: Melbourne's costly loss raises top-8 questions
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne's recent loss has put their top-8 position under real pressure as the AFL finals race enters its crucial phase. The ladder predictor suggests several teams are now locked in a tight battle for the final spots, with Melbourne's percentage and upcoming fixtures now under the microscope. The AFL finals picture is rapidly crystallising with only a handful of rounds left in the regular season.
